timeline.text: Launches as part of the FCDO development impact bond pilot, with outcome payers paying through a trustee.
The programme reaches households in 241 villages, while 241 control villages are held back for comparison.
An endline survey of 9,888 households finds positive, statistically significant gains in consumption and net assets.
The final report is published, and the outcome payment maxes out at US$4,280,618.

deck.caption:
What does it take to get paid only for results?

Village Enterprise ran Africa’s first development impact bond for poverty, and it earned every dollar on offer.

Between late 2017 and 2020, it delivered its one-year poverty graduation programme in 241 villages in western Kenya and eastern Uganda, with 241 more held back for comparison. Outcome payers paid only for measured gains in household consumption and net assets.

In 2021, IDinsight’s randomised evaluation of 9,888 households found positive and statistically significant gains on both. The full outcome payment of about US$4.28 million was earned.

The lesson? Paying for results works when everyone agrees up front what success looks like and how it will be measured. And a bond pays for one round: the next payer still has to be found.
